controls.reason: Each defect in the authoritative ledger can be checked for the ten exact affected-scope, impact, workaround and ownership fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A defect missing customer exposure data, affected versions or owner leaves a deterministic schema or registry-join failure.

controls.reason: When possible is a contextual exception, and reproduction occurrence does not prove the defect was exercised against the truly affected released artifact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team can declare exact-artifact reproduction impossible and use a convenient build even though the release image is available and behaves differently.

controls.reason: Several counts and times are computable, but escaped defects, recurrence and complete customer exposure depend on discovering and linking all real failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The dashboard can report all eight measures while an unreported customer defect and a semantically recurring issue are absent from the ledger.

controls.reason: Determining which of five assurance failures caused a defect requires causal analysis, production representativeness judgment and evidence interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A review can check every category and blame a missing assertion while the real cause was an unrealistic production model.

controls.reason: Artifact edits are observable, but deciding how lessons should change seven practices and whether the changes embody the lesson is contextual.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All seven artifacts can receive superficial updates while the coding rule and runbook still permit the same defect mechanism.

controls.reason: Evidence presence cannot demonstrate corrective-action effectiveness without a causal protocol, observation horizon and recurrence oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A corrective action can close after one passing test while the defect still recurs under an untested production condition.

controls.reason: A release gate can join the authoritative critical-item registry to current, unexpired verification-evidence identities and block any missing edge.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical journey or mandatory standard with stale or absent evidence creates a deterministic no-go condition.

controls.reason: Exact artifact, configuration, schema, flag, environment and dependency identities can be bound to both test results and the release manifest.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Any mismatch in the six identities fails the provenance equality check and blocks the release.

controls.reason: The required-test ledger can deterministically reject skipped, suppressed, quarantined or retry-only passes lacking an approved retry explanation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A required test hidden in quarantine or passing only after an unexplained rerun cannot reach the release-approved state.

controls.reason: The evidence package can be validated for the fourteen exact strategy, scope, traceability, execution, result, limitation and approval artifact classes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting test data, exclusions or approvals breaks the signed package manifest and its finite completeness schema.

controls.reason: For every policy-tagged high-impact item, the package can require either immutable raw evidence or an independently replayable evidence recipe.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A high-impact resilience experiment with only a summary and no raw trace or reproducible recipe fails the exact evidence alternative.

controls.reason: No bounded source establishes all insufficiently tested defect classes and conditions; a document can only list recognized gaps.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The document can contain several gap classes while omitting the very failure condition the team has not modeled.

controls.reason: Monitoring and incident-response records do not prove they can detect and contain every risk that preproduction testing could not cover.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A detector and runbook can exist while an untested risk emits no signal or exceeds the containment path's authority.

controls.reason: The rule requires interpreting whether the final assurance prose presents testing as proof that no defects exist; a policy or phrase list cannot decide that meaning.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A statement can avoid banned literal phrases yet still imply that testing proves the release defect-free, so a bounded record or token check can pass while the rule is broken.

controls.reason: A versioned assurance-scope record can define the nine finite qualities, harms, obligations, claims, systems and context dimensions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If users, versions or operating conditions lack scope definitions, the exact nine-dimension schema fails.

controls.reason: A stakeholder list cannot prove every relying person or organization and supported decision was discovered, especially external or indirect reliance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All known stakeholders can be mapped while a regulator, customer operator or downstream decision maker remains omitted.

controls.reason: An evidence schema can require each item to use one of four distinct types: implementation, operation, outcome or absence of known failure.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An outcome record mislabeled as implementation evidence or an untyped item violates the exact enum and case schema.

controls.reason: A versioned independence policy can define requirements for the six finite activities: design review, verification, validation, audit, certification and risk acceptance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If certification or risk acceptance lacks an independence rule, the exact activity-policy mapping fails.

controls.reason: Fields can exist, but completeness of limitations, exclusions, assumptions and dependencies is open-ended and freshness can depend on undiscovered changes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every section can be populated while a material supplier assumption and its resulting stale evidence remain unrecorded.

controls.reason: Materiality, clarity, boundedness and testability are semantic qualities requiring expert interpretation rather than record-field presence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim can have scope and test fields yet remain vague about acceptable harm and therefore not be meaningfully testable.

controls.reason: Each assurance claim can be checked for exact system, release, configuration, environment, period and operational-context identities.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim missing its configuration digest or covered period fails the finite six-field scope binding.

controls.reason: Whether a claim is broad, decomposition is complete and subclaims are independently supportable requires argument and domain judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A broad safety claim can be split into two syntactically separate subclaims that share the same unsupported assumption.

controls.reason: A case can list five argument fields without proving all assumptions and dependencies or that inference rules capture the real reasoning.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every section can exist while a hidden independence assumption makes the conclusion invalid.

controls.reason: Graph completeness can prove that each subclaim has an edge, but the rule also requires the linked evidence to be relevant, which needs contextual interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unrelated artifact can be labeled supports and satisfy every referential-integrity check while leaving the subclaim substantively unsupported.

controls.reason: The typed assurance graph can forbid any evidence path that cycles back to the same claim, making circular support exactly detectable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim directly or transitively used as its own evidence creates a graph cycle and cannot pass.

controls.reason: Claim records can use distinct, nonoverlapping types for design intent and deployed behavior with type-specific evidence authorities.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A deployed-behavior conclusion supported only as design intent fails the claim-type and authority schema.

controls.reason: The claim schema can distinguish expected behavior from demonstrated behavior and require result evidence only for the demonstrated type.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Relabeling a specification as a demonstrated observation violates the exact evidence-authority constraint.

controls.reason: An assurance case can be content-versioned and cryptographically bound to immutable release and evidence identifiers.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Changing the release artifact or an evidence item invalidates the stored digests and case binding.

controls.reason: Evidence acceptance criteria can be versioned and timestamped before the earliest result that relies on them.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Criteria created after a test result or absent from its evidence type fail the temporal and registry checks.

controls.reason: Prefer is not a deterministic obligation, and representativeness of a nonproduction configuration requires contextual similarity and risk judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team can claim preference while repeatedly accepting evidence from a convenient configuration that omits a production-only dependency.

controls.reason: Each evidence record can be checked for the ten exact provenance, execution-context, scope and result fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing tool version, operator, data identity or execution time creates an exact schema failure.

controls.reason: A content-addressed provenance graph can require an unbroken chain through requirement, source, build, deployment, execution and observation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An observation not linked to its deployed artifact or build source leaves a deterministic missing edge.

controls.reason: Structured records cannot prove protection against every unauthorized alteration or deletion path across evidence stores, backups and administrators.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Signed evidence can reveal modification yet a privileged recovery account can delete both an item and its unreplicated index.

controls.reason: Materiality, correct calibration, substantive tool validation and completeness of known limitations require technical judgment and independent standards.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record can show current calibration and validation while the procedure uses an inappropriate reference range and misses a material bias.

controls.reason: Every evidence item in the ledger can retain immutable content and disposition even when failed, inconclusive, excluded or superseded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Deleting a failed result or superseding it without a disposition breaks the append-only ledger chain.

controls.reason: A versioned policy can assign explicit validity periods and invalidating event types to each evidence class.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An evidence class without expiry or stale-event rules fails the finite policy mapping.

controls.reason: Materiality and complete detection of source, dependency, configuration, data, environment, threat and usage changes are contextual and unbounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured events can recollect evidence while an indirect dependency update is missed or a usage change is wrongly deemed immaterial.

controls.reason: Future retrievability and interpretability for the full required period depend on storage survival, formats, tools and changing retention authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Evidence can be readable today while its proprietary decoder or encryption key becomes unavailable before retention ends.

controls.reason: Failure-consequence classification for all components, data and decisions requires complete inventory plus safety, security and business judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every registered item can receive a class while an omitted function or understated compromise consequence produces a false pass.

controls.reason: For every registered integrity class, a policy can define the five exact rigor, independence, coverage, formality and retention requirements.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A class missing mathematical rigor rules or evidence retention fails the finite class-policy join.

controls.reason: A versioned policy can define exact triggering conditions for formal methods, exhaustive analysis, proof, model checking and justified bounds.
controls.counterexample_analysis: If model checking has no applicability condition, the five-method policy matrix is incomplete.

controls.reason: Review records do not prove every relevant architecture, exposure, user or consequence change was detected and correctly recognized as affecting classification.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All tracked change events can trigger review while an unrecorded exposure change leaves the integrity class stale.

controls.reason: An assurance-activity registry can assign each activity an allowed self-review or required independent-review mode under versioned policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An activity requiring independence but approved solely by its performer violates the exact activity-policy join.

controls.reason: Identity and responsibility records can deterministically prevent the sole delivery owner from being the only approver of policy-tagged material residual risk.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A material risk with one approver who is its sole delivery owner fails the separation-of-approval constraint.

controls.reason: Access grants can be recorded, but complete evidence and source availability plus access to all relevant environments and personnel are open-ended.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A reviewer can have the listed permissions while a supplier artifact or key operator needed for the review remains unavailable.

controls.reason: Only the reviewer can authoritatively disclose personal conflicts, incentives, prior involvement and relationships; records cannot prove absence of undisclosed conflicts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every form can be complete while a reviewer hides a supplier financial relationship.

controls.reason: Whether independence is impaired and whether recusal, rotation or supplementation restores it requires accountable organizational judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A reviewer can be supplemented on paper while retaining decisive influence despite a serious conflict.

controls.reason: Reviewer competence in a system, assurance method and domain is a human qualification and performance judgment, not a schema fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Certificates and experience fields can be complete while the reviewer lacks practical competence for the specialized method.

controls.reason: A record cannot prove that every dissenting opinion and unresolved finding was voiced and preserved; human participants control disclosure.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The decision file can retain submitted dissent while a reviewer is pressured not to record a material objection.

controls.reason: Every policy-tagged material adverse conclusion can require a management identity, explicit response text, disposition and timestamp.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An adverse conclusion with silence or an implicit approval has no linked response and fails the ledger join.

controls.reason: Determining when advisory involvement compromises audit or certification objectivity is a professional, regulatory and conflict-of-interest judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Separate team names can appear in records while shared incentives and prior design responsibility still compromise independence.

controls.reason: Periodicity can be scheduled, but provider quality, consistency and missed-defect patterns require outcome interpretation and an incomplete defect oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider can receive strong scores from recorded reviews while repeatedly missing a defect class that has not yet been recognized.

controls.reason: A conformance claim can be checked for exact normative requirement identity, version, profile, scope and selected options.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim missing its profile or using an unversioned standard fails the six-part normative binding.

controls.reason: Every claimed requirement in the sealed conformance profile can be joined to evidence and an explicit disposition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claimed requirement without evidence or disposition creates a deterministic missing mapping.

controls.reason: The conformance record can require finite sections for permitted deviations, extensions, optional features and inherited controls.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting an enabled optional feature or recorded deviation breaks the exact four-section profile schema.

controls.reason: Interoperability test occurrence cannot prove independent implementations work together across all operations, versions, states and platforms.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two implementations can pass a handshake fixture while failing an untested migration or error-recovery interaction.

controls.reason: Whether exclusions invalidate the intended conformance claim is a semantic and sometimes legal interpretation of normative requirements.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record can mark an exclusion harmless while it removes a mandatory capability central to the advertised profile.

controls.reason: An audit or certificate record can require explicit start and end time plus the exact covered product-version set.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A certificate lacking a covered version or period fails the finite scope schema.

controls.reason: A certificate register can track expiry, surveillance, conditions, exceptions and renewal obligations as five exact state fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A certificate with an unrecorded renewal duty or expired surveillance date fails the registry rules.

controls.reason: Materiality and certification impact of architecture, supplier, location, process and product changes require assessor and regulatory judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A reassessment form can exist while a significant supplier-location change is misclassified as immaterial and outside certificate scope.

controls.reason: Identifying every assurance claim dependent on five external-control categories requires a complete claim and dependency graph that its own records cannot prove.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered links can be present while an open-source transitive dependency or customer-operated control is omitted.

controls.reason: Correctly drawing inherited, shared and direct control boundaries depends on contracts, architecture and responsibility interpretation, not labels alone.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every control can receive one label while a shared supplier responsibility is incorrectly assigned as inherited and leaves a gap.

controls.reason: Supplier assurance scope fields can be exactly compared with the consumed service, region, data class, configuration and usage period records.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An attestation for another region or configuration fails the five-dimensional scope intersection.

controls.reason: Monitoring all supplier changes, incidents, expired attestations and scope reductions requires complete suppliers and external publication channels.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured feeds can be current while a subcontractor incident or private scope reduction is never received.

controls.reason: A clause label cannot prove that contracts provide enforceable evidence availability and transition rights; legal scope and remedies require counsel.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A contract can contain both headings while exceptions make the rights unusable during termination.

controls.reason: Which unavailable evidence requires compensation and whether a control adequately compensates are contextual risk and assurance judgments.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every missing artifact can link to a control while the control does not address the lost assurance property.

controls.reason: For every registered assurance claim, a policy can define production indicators explicitly typed as supporting or challenging evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim with no challenge indicator or an untyped metric fails the exact claim-to-indicator mapping.

controls.reason: Relevant outcomes and effective monitoring across nine quality domains require contextual applicability and complete telemetry and behavior coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Nine dashboards can exist while an inaccessible workflow or privacy harm emits no monitored signal.

controls.reason: Determining which claims seven operational-event types affect requires causal and semantic impact judgment beyond record linking.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded incident can link to a claim while a complaint revealing an invalid assumption is linked to the wrong conclusion.

controls.reason: Recognizing that operational evidence contradicts an assumption is semantic reasoning; a workflow can only enforce reopening after that judgment is made.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A production metric can directly falsify an assumption yet remain unflagged, so no automatic reopen occurs.

controls.reason: Complete configuration and deployment change detection plus correct evidence-impact analysis cannot be proved from configured change records.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known changes can invalidate evidence while an out-of-band flag or deployment mutation is missed.

controls.reason: Where risk warrants control testing and what continuous or scheduled cadence is adequate require risk and threshold judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical control can receive a rare scheduled test after being rated low risk without sound justification.

controls.reason: Enough telemetry to evaluate trends and reconstruct historical claim validity is an open-ended sufficiency and interpretability judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Retention can meet a stated duration while missing event dimensions needed to test a past assurance assumption.

controls.reason: Major changes, new threats and changed obligations require contextual or legal recognition, and complete external event detection is unbounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Recorded incidents can trigger review while a new applicable threat or obligation is missed or deemed nonmajor.

controls.reason: When an obligation ends and which retention requirements still apply require legal authority and contextual system-lifecycle interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A closed-service record can trigger deletion while a regulatory evidence-retention duty remains in force.

controls.reason: Every assurance case tagged material can require a completed, versioned challenge-review record with reviewer and challenged-claim identities.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A material case lacking challenge review or using a review of another version fails the exact ledger join.

controls.reason: Claim precision, evidence relevance, argument validity and limitation visibility are substantive argument-quality judgments, not field-presence facts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A neatly structured case can link irrelevant evidence through an invalid inference while every section appears complete.

controls.reason: Open defects and exceptions can be joined to the assurance case, but whether each is meaningfully reflected in claim scope and confidence requires semantic judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every open item can have a case link while the claim text and conclusion ignore its actual impact.

controls.reason: A release gate can map criticality, evidence freshness, defeater resolution and independence policy states to mandatory no-go outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical unsupported claim, stale evidence, open defeater or policy-failing reviewer state cannot pass the exact gate table.

controls.reason: The decision ledger can record actor identity and one of five exact actions: review, challenge, approve, reject or conditional accept.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An approval without reviewer identity or an untyped conditional decision fails the finite event schema.

controls.reason: The exact assurance-case digest can be preserved and bound to the released artifact and production-configuration digests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Changing the case, artifact or configuration breaks the three-way immutable identity binding.

controls.reason: A provisional-claim policy can define the exact required post-release observations and require them before the final transition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Finalizing with a missing observation or before its bounded window closes violates the state-transition guard.

controls.reason: Approval state can deterministically revoke when a versioned required condition, monitoring check or compensating-control state becomes failed.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A failed required control with approval still active violates the exact dependency-triggered revocation rule.
